A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaussianBlock. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained content and identifying additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction metrics, decomposition and editing results, and component and hyperparameter ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds qualitative failure cases, a resolution comparison, and multi-view reconstruction and editing results.

M1.justification: The two-stage pipeline, attention-guided centering loss, dynamic splitting/fusion, Gaussian binding/inheritance, and optimization objectives are retained. The additional resolution experiment does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The named benchmark coverage remains unchanged. Section 7.3 and Figure 7(a) add qualitative testing of detailed outdoor structures, including woods and leaves, extending evaluation to failure scenarios that v1 discussed only generally as a background limitation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: EMS and DBW in Table 1; 3DGS, OmniSeg3D, and DBW in Table 2; and the same qualitative comparators in Figures 1 and 3, including GaussianEditor in Figure 1.

E3.justification: Figure 7(b) introduces a comparison between two superquadric resolutions labeled Level 1 and Level 2. Existing metrics, preprocessing, optimization budgets, and other settings match between v1 Section 6.1 and v3 Section 7.1. Exact mesh resolutions for the added comparison are unspecified.

E4.justification: v3 adds qualitative failure analysis for detailed structures and a primitive-resolution sensitivity comparison in Sections 7.3–7.4 and Figure 7. The existing component and hyperparameter ablations in Tables 3–4 and Figure 5 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added qualitative results introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results, including GaussianBlock's reported CD of 3.69 and DTU PSNR of 30.7. v3 adds qualitative failure, resolution, and multi-view results in Figures 7–9, and Figure 4 replaces the cans-editing example with a Smurf-editing example.

T1.justification: The mathematical construction and Algorithms 1–3 remain substantively unchanged, with no added proofs or theoretical results. The vertex indexing and product-notation edits in Section 3.1 clarify existing formulas.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about semantically coherent, editable part-level representations combining superquadrics and Gaussians with high fidelity. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The original object-centric/background limitation is retained. Section 7.3 connects specific detailed-structure failures to coarse superquadric representations, while Section 7.4 adds discussion of resolution-related fidelity, computational and memory costs, and fairness to the baseline.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code repository address to the abstract and clarifies the triangle-orientation construction in Section 3.4. Previously disclosed hyperparameters, training schedules, hardware, and training time remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked repository's contents.

R1.justification: The reference set and substantive positioning relative to primitive-based reconstruction, segmentation-based decomposition, and 3D editing remain unchanged. Citation-format edits and repeated attribution to GaussianAvatars do not alter that positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes local wording, grammar, notation-explanation, and cross-reference edits while retaining the main narrative. It updates author and publication information, adds acknowledgments, and combines the splitting/fusion appendix subsections before the new supplementary sections.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands visual documentation through a failure/resolution figure and separate multi-view reconstruction and editing grids in Figures 7–9. It also replaces an example in Figure 4 and rearranges the existing figures and tables around their discussions, while retaining the numerical table structures.

improvement.justification: The added failure demonstrations, resolution discussion, and multi-view results make the method's capabilities and boundaries easier to assess, while the code link improves access information. The gains are limited: the main quantitative evidence is unchanged, and the resolution study provides neither quantitative accuracy/cost measurements nor a detailed experimental setup.
